figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Classiﬁcation, structural analysis, and proposed biosynthesis of cephalotane-type diterpenoids. a) Representative cephalotane-type
diterpenoids concerned in this study, for which a total synthesis had been reported, were marked with a red triangle. b) Classiﬁcation of
cephalotane-type diterpenoids. The family was categorised into ﬁve structural scaﬀolds: cephalotane diterpenoids (type I), Cephalotaxus troponoids
(type II), tropone-free 19-nor-cephalotane diterpenoids (type III), benzenoid cephalotane norditerpenoids (type IV), and miscellaneous cephalotane
diterpenoid variants (type V). The pie chart illustrated the distribution of the 107 known natural products among these types (Figure S1). c) Analysis
of oxidation frequency for each carbon position across the 107 known cephalotane natural products. Carbon positions exhibiting a particularly high
frequency (over 100) of oxidation were highlighted, with the count shown in blue and the corresponding carbon number in red. d) Detailed analysis of
oxidation patterns at key positions (C5, C13, C17, and C19) within the prevalent type I scaﬀold. e) Proposed biosynthetic pathway leading to the ﬁve
distinct cephalotane scaﬀolds. Key transformations investigated in this study were indicated with red stars.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Transcriptomic and phylogenetic analysis of candidate CYP450 genes from cephalotane diterpenoids-producing species. a) Mining of
candidate CYP450 genes by co-expression analysis. A co-expression analysis was performed across a transcriptomic dataset from multiple tissues
using CsCTS as the bait gene. CYP450 genes were ranked by their Pearson’s correlation coeﬃcient (PCC) with CsCTS, and the top 22 genes
(PCC > 0.7) were selected as candidates. Expression values within the heat map represented log2-transformed for a given transcript. The numbers 1,
3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, and 11 in the tissue sample designations represent the speciﬁc months in which the corresponding samples were collected from C.
sinensis plants (leaf and stem). b) Phylogenetic analysis of candidate CYP450 genes together with known CYP450s involved in paclitaxel biosynthesis.
The phylogenetic tree was constructed using the bootstrap neighbour-joining method implemented in MEGA7 with default settings. The percentage
of bootstraps was calculated by 1000 repeats. Genes shown in red were identiﬁed as functional cephalotane diterpenoid biosynthetic genes (this
study). Genes in blue were functional paclitaxel biosynthetic genes. GenBank accession: T2αH (AY518383.2), T5αH (AY741375.1), T7βH (FJ469576.1),
T9αH (PP197199.1), T10βH (AY907826.1), T13αH (AY056019.1), and T14βH (MH497022.1).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. 13,17-Lactone ring formation mediated by CsCYP1 and CsCYP2. a) Total ion chromatograms (TICs) of extracts from N. benthamiana leaves
transiently expressing (i) DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS, (ii) DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS + CsCYP1, (iii) DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS + CsCYP2, and (iv)
DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS + CsCYP1 + CsCYP2, detected by GC-MS. The results indicated the consumption of substrate 6 and the generation of
products 7–10. b) TICs of extracts from N. benthamiana leaves transiently expressing (i) empty vector and (ii) CsCYP2 with co-inﬁltration of substrate
7, detected by GC-MS. c) Scheme illustrating the biosynthetic pathway converting substrate 6 into products 7–10, catalysed by CsCYP1 and/or
CsCYP2. Compounds 7–10, which have not been previously reported in Cephalotaxus plants, were structurally characterised using EI-MS, HRESIMS,
and 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopic analyses.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. 5,19-Lactone ring formation catalysed by CsCYP3. a) Total ion chromatograms (TICs) of extracts from N. benthamiana leaves transiently
expressing (i) DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS, and (ii) DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS + CsCYP3, detected by GC-MS. The results indicated the consumption of
substrate 6 and the generation of products 11–13. The dashed boxes indicated enlargement of the results within speciﬁc time ranges. b) HPLC
chromatograms (λ = 254 nm) of extracts from N. benthamiana leaves transiently expressing (i) DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS, and (ii)
DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS + CsCYP3. The results indicated the generation of products 14, 15, and 16. c) Schematic illustration of the reaction of the
converting 6 into products 11–16 catalysed by CsCYP3. Compounds 11–16, which have not been previously reported in Cephalotaxus plants, were
structurally characterised using EI-MS, ESI-MS, HRESIMS, and 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopic analyses. d) Extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) of
extracts from N. benthamiana leaves transiently expressing (i) empty vector, and (ii) CsCYP3 with co-inﬁltration of substrate 10. The results indicated
the consumption of substrate 10 and the generation of product mannolide 3. EIC for 3 (m/z [M + H]+ = 329.1747). e) Schematic illustration of the
conversion of 10 into 3 catalysed by CsCYP3. Compound 3, previously reported nature product, was structurally conﬁrmed by HRESIMS, 1D NMR
spectroscopic data, and X-ray single crystal diﬀraction analyses (accession No. CCDC2445559).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. The tropone formation mediated by CsCYP4 and the conversion of 5 to 2 by CsCYP3. a) Extracted ion chromatograms (EICs) of extracts from
N. benthamiana leaves transiently expressing (i) empty vector, and (ii) CsCYP4 with co-inﬁltration of substrate 3. The results indicated the
consumption of substrate 3 and the generation of products 4 and 5. EICs for mannolide A 4 (m/z [M + H]+ = 345.1697) and cephinoid H 5 (m/z
[M + H]+ = 297.1485). b) EICs of extracts from N. benthamiana leaves transiently expressing (i) empty vector, and (ii) CsCYP4 with co-inﬁltration of
substrate 4. The results indicated the consumption of substrate 4 and the generation of product 5. c) Scheme illustrating the conversion of 3 to 5 via
CsCYP4 catalysis. 4 and 5 were also detected in N. benthamiana leaves co-expression of DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS + CsCYP1–CsCYP4 (Figure S15) and
were structurally identiﬁed as previously reported nature products by HRESIMS and 1D NMR spectroscopic analyses. d) EICs of extracts from N.
benthamiana leaves transiently expressing (i) empty vector, and (ii) CsCYP4 with co-inﬁltration of substrate 4. The results indicated the generation of
intermediates 4a, 4b, and 4d. EICs for 4a/4b (m/z [M + H]+ = 361.1646) and 4d (m/z [M + H]+ = 315.1591). e) Hypothetic biosynthetic pathway from
4 to 5 via CsCYP4 catalysis. f) EICs of extracts from N. benthamiana leaves transiently expressing (ii) empty vector, and (iii) CsCYP3 with co-inﬁltration
of substrate 5. The results indicated the consumption of substrate 5 and the generation of product 2, with product 2 being present at a higher yield in
the experimental group compared to the control group. g) MS/MS (20 to 50 eV) spectra of hainanolidol 2 produced in N. benthamiana (blue)
compared to the standard (red). h). Schematic illustration of the conversion of 5 to 2 catalysed by CsCYP3. EIC for 2 (m/z [M + H]+ = 313.1434).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. De novo biosynthesis of representative cephalotane-type diterpenoids. a) Schematic representation of the biosynthetic pathway from GGPP
to compounds 6, 7, 10, 3–5, and 2. b) Integrated peak area of extracted ion chromatograms (EIC) for products produced in N. benthamiana after
co-expression with diﬀerent enzyme combinations: (i) DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS; (ii) DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS + CsCYP1; (iii)
DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS + CsCYP1 + CsCYP2; (iv) DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS + CsCYP1 + CsCYP2 + CsCYP3; and (v)
DXS + GGPPS + CsCTS + CsCYP1 + CsCYP2 + CsCYP3 + CsCYP4. Values and error bars represent the mean and the standard error of the mean
(n = 7 biological replicates). Compound 6 was detected by GC-MS, and others were detected by HRESIMS. Representative chromatograms are
shown in Figure S19.
